questions: Are you fully conscious and aware during the movements?
Can you stop the movements voluntarily?
Are the movements occurring only on one side of your body?
Have you had any weakness or numbness in that leg?
Have you had any loss of bladder or bowel control during an episode?
Have you bitten your tongue during an episode?
Do you become confused or unusually sleepy afterward?
Do you have pain, swelling, redness, or warmth in the affected leg?
Do the movements improve when you voluntarily move or walk the leg?
Have you had similar episodes before?
Have you ever had a seizure or other neurologic disorder?
Have you recently started, stopped, or changed any medications?
Have you recently used alcohol, recreational drugs, or stimulants?
Do you have a fever or a recent infection?

DIAGNOSIS: Functional neurological symptom disorder presenting as functional right hemichorea–hemiballismus

ALTERNATIVE 1: Autoimmune hemichorea, particularly systemic lupus erythematosus or antiphospholipid-associated chorea

ALTERNATIVE 2: Wilson disease
